Kieran Zhang 
AI-native indie developer · Nanjing, China 
Before joining Huawei in 2022, I started out at a small company. The years since have mostly been about IDEs and developer tools — language services for a homegrown programming language, IDE integration and performance tuning for HarmonyOS, and bringing AI into mobile development, testing, ops, and troubleshooting. If the years taught me one thing, it is this: in software engineering, everything is a trade-off.
In 2026 I left to build my own products. Not out of disillusionment with big tech — just that in the AI era, what a single person can make has grown far beyond what it used to be.
Off the clock I like taking problems apart the analytic-philosophy way, while leaning more and more on the practical, this-worldly side of Confucian thought. Writing is how I think things through — hence this place. 
 GitHub Twitter Email RSS 
Reading lately 
 Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus · Ludwig Wittgenstein Where the line falls between what can be said and what cannot. 
 The Book of Elon: A Guide to Purpose and Success · Eric Jorgenson Musk's mental models in his own words — reasoning from first principles, not another biography. 
Around me 
Off-screen, I carry a Nikon Z5 II around to shoot, with the odd game of Texas hold'em.

Projects 
A pragmatist with an obsession for aesthetics — I strive to craft products that are both beautiful and functional, and document the practices and results here. 
Pace building 
The desktop GUI for the Pi coding agent: sessions, trajectories, token and cost truth, and extension-registered panels. 
Move at your own pace. 
Pi is a terminal coding agent with a VS Code-style extension system: packages contribute tools, commands, skills, prompts and themes. Pace carries that flexibility to the desktop, so a developer can shape an agent client that is truly their own instead of renting one. 
Pace is not a fork of Pi and not a second runtime. Pi's local session log stays the single source of truth; Pace only projects Pi's event stream into a journal and renders everything from it: the live chat, the Trajectory view of chain of thought and tool calls, and per-turn token and cost accounting. The backend runs in a separate Electron utility process, so heavy log parsing can never make the window stutter. 
Electron · React 19 · TypeScript · Bun · Pi SDK 
 GitHub Website 
Voily building 
Open-source macOS voice-to-text app that turns raw voice into refined text at your cursor. 
Just speak. We'll handle the rest. 
Voily is a voice input method for macOS: press one key, speak, and polished text lands wherever your cursor is. If you can type there, you can speak there — Slack, Cursor, Gmail, ChatGPT, any app that takes text. 
Instead of raw dictation, Voily runs your speech through an AI rewrite pipeline, so what lands is refined text rather than a literal transcript. It sits quietly in the menu bar, always ready behind a single hotkey. 
Swift · macOS · Sparkle 
 GitHub Website 
Pi Index shipped 
A curated list of Pi coding agent extensions, themes, skills and prompt templates, with a searchable companion site. 
Make Pi fit you. 
Pi's package ecosystem grew past five thousand entries fast, and the official registry tells you what exists but not what is worth installing. Pi Index is the community-maintained shortlist: extensions, skills, themes and prompt templates, grouped by what they do, each with a one-line pitch and the install command. 
The list lives as a plain README so anyone can send a pull request. The companion site renders the same data with category filters, search, and copy-to-install buttons, in English and Chinese. It is the most-starred repository I maintain and the entry point I hand to people who ask how to set up Pi. 
Markdown · Astro · Vercel

SubWorth building 
An open benchmark measuring what AI coding subscriptions actually deliver, in dollars of equivalent API usage. 
Check your sub's worth. 
Providers advertise subscriptions as "5x Pro" or "20x Pro" but never say how many dollars that is. About Pi Index 
Kieran maintains Pi Index, an independent directory of Pi Coding Agent packages. It is not affiliated with Pi. Corrections go through GitHub issues. 
Who maintains it 
Kieran maintains the site and the public list. The GitHub account is bubbleptr, and the list lives in the awesome-pi repository. There is no contact email. Additions and corrections go through issues on that repository. 
 Kieran on GitHub ↗ 
 Kieran on X ↗ 
 awesome-pi repository ↗ 
What is listed 
The directory is the bilingual list in the repository. Each entry has a name, a link, an English description, a Chinese description, and an install command when the project publishes one. The site does not build if a translation is missing or the install commands disagree. 
A few packages, categories, and topics also have a guide. A guide is a source review pinned to a version and a commit, not a second copy of the directory line. The check itself is described in How we pick and verify . 
Not part of Pi 
 Pi is the terminal coding harness published by earendil-works. Pi Index is a separate directory. A listing is not an official Pi release and is not an endorsement. 
Submit or correct 
Open a GitHub issue to add a resource, fix a description, or challenge a guide. Pull requests that follow the list format are welcome too. Issues are the contact channel. 
 Open an issue ↗

sites.title: PiNomad — the durable coding agent for your own machine
sites.description: PiNomad is a self-hosted coding agent built on Pi Durable. It checkpoints every model and tool call, so a crash or restart picks up where it stopped; the Mac app, the web client, and the iPhone app all attach to the same runs.
sites.home_text:
Skip to content 
 PiNomad 
The durable coding agent for your own machine. 
 PiNomad runs on your machine, with that machine's shell and repos, and checkpoints every
 model and tool call. If the host crashes or restarts, the run picks up where it stopped.
 The Mac app, the web client, and the iPhone app all attach to the same runs.
 Get started 
 View on GitHub 
 Use any model pi supports 
Anthropic 
OpenAI 
Google 
DeepSeek 
xAI 
Mistral 
Qwen 
Kimi 
Z.AI 
MiniMax 
OpenRouter 
GitHub Copilot 
17 more 
Any screen 
Step away from your desk 
 Start a task at your desk, then check on it or steer it from your phone. Devices pair
 with a one-time QR code and talk to the host over an end-to-end encrypted channel.
 Direct over your LAN or tailnet 
 Relay that only sees ciphertext 
 Screenshot coming: the same run on iPhone. 
Durable runs 
Runs survive crashes and restarts 
 Pi Durable writes a checkpoint after every model call and tool call. After a restart
 the run continues from the last one; only the call that was in flight runs again.
 A run drawn as a track of model and tool calls. Each finished call plants a flag. The
 host crashes between two calls; after the restart the run continues from the last
 flag, and only the half-finished call is redone.
 Start a run 
Features 
What the agent can do 
The agent has pi's four tools (read, bash, edit, write), plus: 
A worktree for every conversation 
 In a Git repo each conversation works in its own worktree and branch, so your
 checkout stays untouched.
Questions, not approvals 
 Tools run without approval prompts. When the direction is unclear, the agent asks
 one to four multiple-choice questions.
Subagents and named agents 
 Hand self-contained tasks to subagents that run in parallel, or delegate to a
 reusable role with an @name mention, optionally pinning its model and
 thinking level.
And also 
 Forks 
 Branch off from a message and keep both lines going. 
 codemode 
 The model writes JavaScript that calls other tools in a QuickJS sandbox; only the script's output enters the context. 
 MCP 
 Servers configured in ~/.agents/mcp.json , in the usual mcpServers format. 
 Images 
 Paste, drop, or pick up to 4 images per message in the web and desktop composer. 
 AGENTS.md and skills 
 Reads AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md and skills from ~/.agents and the project, on every request. 
Clients 
Pick up the same run anywhere 
Web 
 Open app.pinomad.si , or the web client your
 host serves itself ( pinomad link ). Any modern browser.
macOS 
 Signed DMG from
 GitHub Releases ;
 updates itself.
 Apple silicon 
iOS 
Pairs with your host by scanning a one-time QR code. 
 Internal TestFlight only for now 
Linux, Windows 
Use the web client. 
Quick start 
Install, start the host, open a client 
The host needs Node 25+ on macOS or Linux. 
 pinomad host uses the models and credentials you set up in pi
 ( ~/.pi/agent ). Haven't set up pi yet? pinomad host --faux "hi" 
 runs a scripted fake model so you can click around.
 It's early. Pi Durable is itself experimental, and the host and its clients must
 speak the same protocol major version.
 Terminal 
 Copy 
 npm i -g pinomad
pinomad host # uses the models and credentials set up in pi 
pinomad link # in another terminal: prints a web client link 
Start a run. Walk away. 
Free and open source. It runs on your hardware, with your model credentials. 
 Get started 
 Star on GitHub
If PiNomad is useful to you, a star helps other people find it.

readmes.bubbleptr/Voily:
Voily

Just speak — we'll do the rest.

简中

--- Voily is an open-source, AI-powered voice input tool for macOS. Press a key, speak naturally, and your words land at the cursor — in any app. It does more than transcribe: an optional LLM cleans up filler, polishes your phrasing, or translates Chinese to English on the fly. The built-in engine runs fully on-device with no API key and no cost; cloud engines are there when you want higher accuracy. One key does it all. ## Why Voily - **Speak faster than you type** — press the trigger key, talk, and text appears right at your cursor: email, editor, chat, terminal, any text field. - **Local-first and private** — the built-in SenseVoice engine runs entirely on-device, with no network calls, no API key, and no per-request cost. - **Translate on the same key** — long-press, speak Chinese, get English at the cursor. No mode switch, no second app. - **Optional AI polish** — let an LLM strip filler words, rewrite into a formal register, or turn dictated steps into a numbered list. - **Stays out of your way** — lives in the menu bar, no Dock icon by default, and mutes system audio while recording to prevent feedback. - **Works where keystrokes fail** — text is injected through the system pasteboard, so it lands reliably in sandboxed apps, password fields, and remote desktops. - **Open source and pluggable** — Apache 2.0, with five ASR engines behind one shared pipeline. ## How It Works Press the trigger key to start recording. Voily captures the microphone, streams audio to a speech recognition engine, optionally refines the result with an LLM, and pastes the final text at your cursor. A floating overlay shows every step — recording, transcribing, refining, injecting — so you always know what's happening. ## Quick Start ### Download Get the latest
readmes.bubbleptr/pace:
Pace

The desktop GUI for the Pi coding agent. Pi's design and flexibility, carried to the desktop.

English | 简体中文

Pi is a coding agent that runs in the terminal, extensible in the spirit of VS Code: packages contribute tools, commands, skills, prompts and themes. Pace brings that flexibility to the desktop, so you can shape a desktop agent that is truly your own. The name comes from *move at your own pace*: developers should keep full ownership of their agent and set their own rhythm. > [!NOTE] > Pace is in early `0.y.z` development. Only the latest version on GitHub Releases is supported. Journal and projection formats may change between minor versions; the in-app updater handles upgrades. Pi's session data is unaffected (see [Local data and recovery](#local-data-and-recovery)).

## Highlights - **Session timeline**: follow the agent's chain of thought and tool calls in order, with token usage and cost for every turn. # dsh-holdem
无限注德州扑克：**1 名玩家 + 5 位 LLM 智能体**。装上后，Web GUI 中间栏会出现「德州扑克」Tab，
会话区域还会浮着一个可拖动、可收起的小窗。
智能体只能看见自己的底牌；桌边闲话是中文，不会泄露推理或手牌。
## 安装
### 桌面版
桌面版（DeepSeek Harness.app）自带一套 dsh CLI，装到它自己的 `desktop` profile：
```sh
"/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh" plugin --profile desktop add dsh-holdem
```
装完桌面版会热重载 profile 并把新的客户端模块推给页面，通常不用重启；如果「德州扑克」Tab 没出现，退出重开桌面版。
### Web
```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-holdem
dsh --profile web
```
装的是 npm 上的预构建包，不用 clone、不用 build、不用 `allowBuilds`。
卸载（把 profile 与 CLI 换成对应的一套）：
```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-holdem
```
## 开发
```sh
pnpm install
pnpm build
```
| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `src/host.js` | Node 半区：牌局引擎 + `/dsh-holdem/*` JSON API；缺模型时回退启发式机器人 |
| `src/client.cjs` | 浏览器半区：`conversation.view` Tab + `shell.overlay` 悬浮小窗 |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | 往 web 组合插入本包 |
改 Host 后需要重启 `dsh --profile web`。改 Client 后重新 `pnpm build`、刷新页面。
## 下注尺度
`legalFor` 的 `maxRaiseTo` 是**智能体的全部筹码**，所以直接把合法区间丢给模型会出事：
模型常在区间里挑一个"看起来挺大"的数，于是每次加注都静默变成全下（上游修过同一类问题的
客户端版本，见 `f90bd7e`）。现在 host 侧统一按底池给尺度：
- prompt 里给的是**底池倍数**区间 `minRaiseTo – currentBet + 3 × 底池`，并单独列出 `allin`
  作为"整副筹码"的显式选项，不再是加注区间的上界。
- 非 `allin` 的加注一律过 `clampRaise`（`src/bets.js`）：落在 `[minRaiseTo, 上限]` 内。
  只有显式选 `allin` 才会推光；底池已经很大时上限自然超过筹码，那时"合法加注就是全下"仍然成立。
- 启发式兜底 `decideAi` 的额度也走同一条钳制——它原先会算出超过自己筹码的加注额，在 LLM
  报错的回退路径上绕过 `normalizeChoice`，等于意外推光。
规则与边界都在 `test/bets.test.mjs`（纯函数）和 `test/ai-sizing.test.mjs`（stub 掉 llm 服务、
离线跑完整 AI 决策链路）里钉住。
## 买入与出局
每人起始 200 万，**外加 3 次买入**（也就是 4 条命）。筹码输光后：
- 下一手开始前自动补回 200 万，日志写明「重新买入 2000000（第 N/3 次）」；
- 3 次用完后再破产就**出局**：bot 坐观退场，不再发牌、不再被收盲注、不再参与行动；
- 你出局则本局结束（`status: 'game-over'`），界面显示结束横幅，只能 `Reset` 再开一桌；
- 桌面上只剩一名玩家时同样结束（等于打通关）。
界面上每个玩家行、每个座位都会显示「买入 N/3」，出局者额外标「出局」并置灰。
出局座位会被盲注与庄家轮转跳过；桌上只剩两人时按单挑规则，**按钮位下小盲**。
这条规则的动机是上游原来是**无限买入**：任何人（包括你）输光都会在下一手被无条件补回
200 万，既无人能出局，全下也就没有任何后果。规则本身是纯函数 `src/table-rules.js`
（`rebuyDecision` / `blindSeats`），单测见 `test/table-rules.test.mjs`；引擎接线与出局座位
的不变量由 `test/rebuys.test.mjs` 覆盖（含一个固定随机种子的「我方四条命耗尽」端到端用例）。
## 亮牌与翻牌动效
一手结束后看得到赢家的底牌：
- **摊牌**：所有没弃牌的人亮牌（弃牌者仍是背面）；
- **无人跟注**：只亮赢家那两张，其余人一律保持隐藏——一手进行中机器人的底牌永远不会下发到

# PiNomad
English · [中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [pinomad.si](https://pinomad.si)
A self-hosted coding agent built on [Pi Durable](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-durable). The agent runs on your own machine; the Mac app, the web client, and the iPhone app all attach to the same runs.
<sub>One run, three clients: Mac app (left), iPhone via iPhone Mirroring (center), web (right). The host is a Linux box on the same tailnet.</sub>
- **Your machine does the work.** The host runs on a Mac mini, a Linux box, or a VPS, and the agent uses that machine's shell and repositories.
- **Runs survive crashes and restarts.** Pi Durable checkpoints every model call and tool call, so a restarted host picks up where it stopped.
- **Clients are just windows.** Start a task at your desk, then check on it or steer it from your phone. Devices pair with a one-time QR code and talk to the host over an end-to-end encrypted channel: directly on your LAN or tailnet, or through a relay that only sees ciphertext.
> **Status:** early and moving fast. Pi Durable is itself experimental, and the host and its clients must speak the same protocol major version.
## Quick start
The host needs Node 25+ on macOS or Linux.
```sh
npm i -g pinomad
pinomad host        # uses the models and credentials you set up in pi (~/.pi/agent)
pinomad link        # in another terminal: prints a browser link to the web client
```
Haven't set up pi yet? `pinomad host --faux "hi"` runs a scripted fake model so you can click around.
## Connect your other devices
Open a port for paired devices, then pair each device with its own QR code:
```sh
pinomad host --remote-port 7422
pinomad pair        # one-time QR code and link, expires after 5 minutes
```
Scan the code with the iPhone app, or paste the link into the Mac app. The remote port accepts paired devices only; revoke them under Settings → Devices.
The pairing link uses the LAN address the host detects. On a tailnet or behind a tunnel, add `--public-url http://<tailnet-ip>:7422` so the link points there. To reach a host at home from anywhere, run the relay on a VPS: see [Remote access](docs/remote-access.md).
